diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, $T$ is also injective. We apply spectral theorem for compact normal operators, see, e.g., \cite[Theorem 12.12]{Alt:2016}, and obtain the result of the lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: The spectral theorem argument for the compact self-adjoint operator T on H^1_0 establishes H^1_0 completeness and H^2-orthogonality, but does not prove that the eigenfunctions form a basis in H^2_0. Later Galerkin estimates explicitly use this H^2_0 basis property to infer H^2_0 stability of P_n and convergence P_n φ -> φ in H^2_0, so a nontrivial completeness argument is missing.

failure_location.quote: and form basis for both $H^2_0(\Omega)$ and $H^1_0(\Omega)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a contained argument proving H^2_0 completeness, for example by showing T^{-1} is self-adjoint in the H^2_0 inner product and applying the spectral theorem to that unbounded self-adjoint operator.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous Galerkin existence proof and subsequent continuous regularity results, as well as the discrete orthogonality and error estimates that rely on them, are unsupported until the H^2_0 completeness of the buckling eigenfunctions is proved.
issues.title: H^2_0 eigenbasis claim not proved
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a nontrivial completeness argument, but it is contained and does not change the stated regularity or error rates if the argument is added.
